To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LP method provides an approximation to the channel model order m significant part of the true channel, the accuracy of the approximation depends on the diversity and size of the mth order significant part and size of the unmodelled tails, and the accuracy of the method is not critically affected by the size of the channel model order significant part, nor by the size of its first term.
the linear prediction method is robust with regard to channel undermodeling, and the performance of the LP method depends on the diversity and the size of unmodeled tails.

(a) LP method is not robust with respect to effective undermodeling and (over)modeling, (b) the LP method is robust to undermodeling of the channel if the channel is sparse, and (c) the performance of LP method is not critically dependent on the size of first impulse response coefficient in realistic scenarios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the robustness of a blind channel identification method in a realistic setting where the channel is not fully known.
the performance of the LP method for blind channel identi cation in the presence of channel undermodeling and/or overmodeling.
the performance of the LP method when there is an effective undermodeling or overmodeling of the true channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LP method performs reasonably well for blind channel identification as long as the effective channel is not severely undermodeled or overmodeled.
the LP method is robust in the sense of (a) and (b) only when the channel is overmodeled and the first impulse response terms are large.
the LP method performs reasonably well in most practical scenarios.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the LP method has been widely used, its performance has not been well studied.

the LP method can be considered a robust channel identification method only when the channel model is close to the true channel in terms of the channel order and the channel order of the first significant part of the true channel.
the LP method is robust with regard to channel undermodeling and overmodeling as long as the unmodeled channel tails are not too large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LP method is a powerful blind channel identification method for channels of order M, even when the channel model is only of order m with m<M.
the LP method should not be used for blind channel identification in practice, unless the order of the true channel is known.
the performance of the LP method depends on the effective order of the channel, which is a function of the channel impulse response, the signal, the additive noise, and the channel model.
